title: Tensor coherence of the pinned pullback composition comparison
statement: Let $g:T\to S$, $h:S\to X$, and $k:T\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $w:h\circ g=k$. Let $M,N$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-module-pullback] and let $\delta_f(P,Q):f^*(P\otimes Q)\to f^*P\otimes f^*Q$ be the canonical tensor comparison with the pinned unit section formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $c_P:g^*h^*P\to k^*P$ for the inverse of the pinned adjunction-mate composition comparison [def-pc-tensor-pullback-composition-iso]. Then the two morphisms from $g^*h^*(M\otimes N)$ to $k^*M\otimes k^*N$ agree: first $g^*(\delta_h)$, then $\delta_g(h^*M,h^*N)$, then $c_M\otimes c_N$ equals first $c_{M\otimes N}$, then $\delta_k(M,N)$. No finiteness, coherence, support or adic hypotheses are imposed.

source.place: Tags 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), 0095 and 0096; tensor coherence needed in the multiplication paragraph of 09ZT. The mate and pure-section calculation is agent-written, from these universal properties. Read https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01CD, /tag/0096 and /tag/09ZT on 2026-10-14.

proof.text: Substitute k = g followed by h. Write ah, ag, ak for the pinned tensor-pullback adjunctions. The unit_conjugateEquiv_symm identity for the defining mate, followed by its inverse and cancellation, says the composite unit followed by the inverse composition comparison equals the unit of ak. On sections the pushforward comparison for this composite is the identity; its equality-transport restriction is the presheaf identity. This is proved as composition_unit_sections.

Apply the composite adjunction Hom bijection to the two sides and use the tensor universal property to test their adjoints on tmulSection(s,t) over every open U. Naturality of the g-unit moves the pullback of the h-tensor comparison through that unit. Apply the pure-section formulas first for h and then for g. The resulting elementary tensor is the tensor of the two successive unit images. Tensoring the inverse composition comparisons and applying the unit identity separately to M and N gives the tensor of the composite-unit images. On the other side apply the unit identity to M tensor N and then the pure-section formula for the composite. The answers agree, proving equality.

theorem finiteStructure_tensorComparison_composition
    {X S T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) (h : S ⟶ X) (k : T ⟶ X)
    (w : g ≫ h = k) (M N : X.Modules) :
    (tensorPullback g).map (Classical.choose (module_pullback_tensor h) M N).hom ≫
        (Classical.choose (module_pullback_tensor g)
          ((tensorPullback h).obj M) ((tensorPullback h).obj N)).hom ≫
        ((tensorPullbackCompositionIso g h k w).inv.app M ⊗ₘ
          (tensorPullbackCompositionIso g h k w).inv.app N) =
      (tensorPullbackCompositionIso g h k w).inv.app (M ⊗ N) ≫
        (Classical.choose (module_pullback_tensor k) M N).hom
